flags.gpt_reasoning: A residential nonpayment pay-or-quit notice under Iowa Code § 562A.27(2) must be served as provided in § 562A.29A. Section 562A.12 is the general notice provision, but § 562A.29A is the specific service statute for termination notices, including nonpayment notices; mail service is not authorized by § 562A.29A(2) alone because subsection (2) governs when mailed notice is deemed completed.
flags.gemini_reasoning: Iowa Code § 562A.29A, titled "Method of service of notice on tenant," is the controlling statute for serving notices in a residential tenancy. Subsection (1) explicitly provides for personal and substituted service, while subsection (2) details a conditional method involving both posting and mailing (certified and first class). The statute cited in the rules file, § 562A.12, is a general definition of "notice" and does not govern the specific procedures for service.

gpt.rationale: For residential tenancies, if rent is unpaid when due, the landlord may terminate the rental agreement only if the tenant fails to pay within three days after written notice of nonpayment and the landlord’s intention to terminate. This statutory three-day notice must precede termination and filing of the eviction action for nonpayment.

gemini.rationale: If rent is unpaid when due, the landlord must give the tenant a written three-day notice of nonpayment and intent to terminate the agreement. If the tenant fails to pay the rent within that three-day period, the landlord may terminate the rental agreement and file for eviction.

federal.name: SCRA § 3951 (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act)
federal.applies_when: Servicemembers and their dependents occupying a residence as their primary dwelling, where the servicemember's military service materially affects their ability to pay the rent.
federal.effect: During a period of military service, a landlord may not evict a servicemember or their dependents from their primary residence without first obtaining a court order. Court may stay proceedings up to 90 days or adjust the rental obligation. Protection applies when monthly rent does not exceed the annual threshold: $4,954.34/month (2024; formula: 130% of BAH for E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area — adjusted annually by DoD). Landlord must file affidavit of non-military-service before default judgment may enter (50 U.S.C. § 3931(b)(1)). FY23 NDAA amendment: replaced CPI-adjusted fixed-dollar threshold with current BAH formula.
federal.statute: 50 U.S.C. § 3951; as amended by Pub. L. 117-263, Div. E, Title LV, § 555 (FY23 NDAA, Dec. 23, 2022)
